quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a way that lets you use your arms to control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body or support your weight.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: Refusing to take a breath test when requested by an officer:

options.text: Is your right and will have no negative consequences.

questions.explanation: When you ride on public roads, you agree to take a chemical test if an officer asks. Refusing a chemical test will result in losing your license for at least one year.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that a winding road is ahead. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. Making a left turn at this intersection is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs are used in construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which of the following should not be done?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider's ability.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan travel based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation for safety.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Stay closer to the vehicle in front of you.
Brake later than you would alone.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, and increase your following distance.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When being passed by another vehicle, be alert to:

options.text: Objects thrown from the other vehicle.
Wind gusts from the passing vehicle.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts from it, and objects that may be thrown from it. Stay alert to all these dangers.

questions.question: When can you carry a passenger?

options.text: Only if the passenger is a child.
Only if the passenger has a motorcycle license.
If your motorcycle is designed to carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: If your motorcycle is designed to carry a passenger.
questions.explanation: You can only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is designed and equipped for it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a stop sign is coming up. Get ready to stop completely before going forward.

questions.question: Which helmet gives you the best protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has been in a previous crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance to more than four seconds?

options.text: When you cannot see past the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions make stopping harder. This includes wet roads, gravel roads, heavy traffic, or when you cannot see ahead.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire went flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the back.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually cannot hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: What should a good face shield NOT be?

options.text: Able to provide clear side views.

questions.explanation: A good face shield must allow air to pass through. An airtight shield can cause fogging and make it hard to see.

questions.question: What should you adjust when carrying a heavy load?
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, springs, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to stop.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. What should you do?

options.text: You do not need to wear bright colors during the day.
You should wear bright colors during the day.
You should wear dark colors during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should wear bright colors during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright colors to make yourself more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: What should you do when nearing a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, position yourself where other drivers can see you most easily.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Change your lane position as needed to see well, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is tailgating you. The other driver may not see the hazard that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light when you are about to slow down in an unexpected place.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do when riding at night?
questions.explanation: Night riding is dangerous because you cannot see as well and other drivers cannot see you. Riders should reduce speed, use full headlights, and increase following distance to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate faster and increases danger. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: When should you use more than a four-second following distance?
questions.explanation: Use a larger following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Use more space on slippery pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent attention than cars. You must check your motorcycle before riding to catch any problems before you enter traffic or ride at high speeds.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Communicate your intentions by using your turn signals and brake light.
Search for hazards in your path.
Hope the other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope the other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers, communicate your intentions, and maintain safe space around you. Search for hazards and be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You are more likely to notice a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Look only at your controls, not ahead.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to communicate. Keep safe space around your motorcycle and scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What usually causes a "wobble" (sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars)?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
Improper tightening of the front wheel to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly shake from side to side. Most wobbles result from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if other cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go slowly through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked line. Only go when it is safe. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop at a point where you can see all traffic.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be ready to act to avoid a hazard.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always make yourself visible to other riders. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation helps riders stay together while keeping safe space around each motorcycle?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of motorcycles to stay close while giving each rider enough space cushion.

questions.question: Impairment from alcohol begins:
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: A proper lane position helps you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Improve your ability to see and be seen.

questions.explanation: Your lane position affects your safety. It helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and set up for turns.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your distance from other vehicles.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down earlier, and increase your distance from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about conditions ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride.

questions.question: After entering a turn, roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
Do not worry about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
questions.explanation: Rolling on the throttle stabilizes your suspension. Maintain a steady speed or accelerate slowly through the turn.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is bright outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
Wear whatever is comfortable, including shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothes when riding so other drivers can see you.
